convoLines.text: "I asked Jorge about what you did with your hands — Jorge's gone. You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Quick version — Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"Drum-Belly — It rears up, belly swelling drum-taut, and beats it with both paws — BOOM. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"I wasn't at that fire," Gloria says. "Whatever was said got said without me in it."
"Still on what you did with your hands. Can't sit still, you know?"
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"Moot talk," Raj says — and the way they say it closes the subject like a door.
"I think — Still on who you don't trust."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"I dreamed Jorge was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
You show them Burdock — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
They relax, a fraction. This is going well.
"I keep turning over the last thing Jorge said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me your trade. I've been watching your hands since — they know things."
"This one — Hanza. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Saw Palmetto. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Why do you ask? Still on that personal stuff."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
You show them Burdock — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "The whole fire was arguing about Lockpick last night — what to even CALL it. 'Ugly-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
«No entiendo nada. ¡Nada!» "No, no." — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
«De acuerdo.» They nod back, slowly.
«Gracias. De verdad, gracias.» (you catch 'Gracias' — thanks) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Eres buena persona.» (you catch 'buena' — good) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «¿Cuántos días llevamos aquí?» (you catch 'días' — days)
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.' We still owe that personal stuff a proper ending, too."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
"What's this about? Still on what's been happening."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Honest. I can work with honest."
"Yeah? What's up? Rest when you can."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
«¿Qué lugar es este? ¿Dónde estamos?» (you catch 'Dónde' — where)
«Es verdad.» (you catch 'verdad' — truth) They nod back, slowly.
«Eres un sol, gracias de corazón.» (You're a sun, thanks from the heart. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«No lo olvidaré.» (I won't forget it. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «¿Tú eres... el jefe?» (Are you... the boss? — you're fairly sure)
"Hm. Almost." Catalina corrects the one word, gently, like setting a bone. "Again." You say it right. They nod, satisfied with both of you.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You said one day at a time. How's that holding — still day by day, or are you thinking further out yet?"
"Take your time."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Beastmaster. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I've been sneaking out at night. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
Kwame has an edge today — something curdled.
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.

A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to prove they're useful. Someone I love needed the lie more than I needed the truth." Quiet. Real.
Kwame looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them Burdock — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
